Got up early last month to see the giant river otters (Pteronura brasiliensis). This family of seven otters was feeding on fish. They are the longest otter species, some measuring as long 5.6 feet. They can be aggressive. Even the caiman generally leave them alone. They are found along rivers in the northern-central Amazon. Many otter families have taken up residence in oxbow lakes along the Amazon river. This family was fishing in an oxbow lake along the Tambopata river. visit markshepherdjournal.com.

Giant River Otters are very fun to watch! Highly social, almost always interacting with other members of the family, we were able to watch them for a good 15 or 20 minutes. They had an island in the middle of the river which they enjoyed playing on, pushing each other off the rocks, or marking territory on the main island. What was interesting was their alarm response (last image), showing them bolt upright in the water, facing off the threat - which in this case was just a large clamp of weeds floating down the river!

As I mentioned on some of the other observations from the River, the locations are fairly approximate as it was difficult to tell exactly where we were! This was the second group of River Otters we saw, with 4 individuals this time.

27-March-2022  I was contacted today by iNaturlaist user setlda, who is the Creator of the Giant Otter Network in Peru.  This organization is dedicated to saving the endangered Giant Otter in Peru.  Initially, they identify individuals like the male Giant Otter in this observation.  This is possible because each otter has a unique pattern of marks on the white patch of its neck.
In her message today, she told me this:  “You might be interested to know, that 2012 is the first year that anyone registered this individual. He appears to have joined the group as an adult and became the reproductive male of the group (the dominant / alpha). I don't have any confirmation yet this year - but as of last year he was still present on in the same location!”  That means that this otter has been in this same location for at least 9 years!
If you want to help with this wonderful project, please contact setlda via her iNaturlaist profile page.

Another group at Encontro das Águas State Park. We watched a member of this group catch a large catfish. Subsequently, there was an altercation over the fish, one individual grabbing at least part of it from the one that caught it--fifth image here.
The sixth image shows the "thief" quite close to the boat. We did not chase, lure them in, or feed them--they seemed to enjoy being near the boats. 
Prey is perhaps a Jaú Catfish (Zungaro species, Pimelodidae).

Giant Otter, Ariranha - Pteronura brasiliensis
It was a real treat to see these, as I had not realized they were found outside of the Amazon Basin. Though globally endangered, they seem to be doing well in Encontro das Águas State Park and showed no fear of the tourist-laden boats. This one was spotted bathing and splashing across the river channel, swam over to investigate us, then caught an eel and consumed it noisily. 

The eel is likely a Marbled Swamp Eel (Synbranchus marmoratus), or a relative.

Ariranha o nutria gigante (Pteronura brasiliensis)

El 14 de agosto de 2026, a las 3:25 p. m., en el Pantanal, observé a dos individuos en aparente comportamiento de apareamiento dentro del agua. El encuentro duró aproximadamente entre cinco y seis minutos.

Durante la interacción, ambos animales se sumergieron y regresaron repetidamente a la superficie, generando bastante movimiento en el agua. Uno de los individuos, aparentemente la hembra, emitió vocalizaciones durante el evento. Los demás integrantes del grupo permanecieron cerca y algunos salieron del agua mientras la pareja continuaba interactuando.

Comportamiento observado: apareamiento, vocalizaciones, inmersiones repetidas y acompañamiento cercano del grupo.
